faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

Run three auto print head alignments.
Make sure High Speed is not selected.
Lower the dpi setting you selected to print.  If you selected 2880 dpi, lower                     the setting to 1440 dpi.

To switch between the two types of black ink, you must use the Black Ink Conversion Kit (included with the printer) and run the Black Ink Change from the user control panel. See
Changing the Black Ink Cartridge

faqs.question: I see the message Service Request 00010004 - 000101D. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Service Request errors in the range 00010004 - 000101D are related to a carriage movement problem. In some instances like paper jams, the carriage locking tab may be partially pushed in, causing the carriage locking mechanism to put a drag on the carriage or lock the carriage completely. This will cause a carriage error. Make sure the carriage locking tab is pulled to the left. Then turn the printer's power off and release the carriage by pushing down on the cutter blade. Slide the carriage to the left and look for any paper that also may be restricting the carriage from moving freely.
00010004
CR Motor encoder check error
00010005
CR Motor out of step
00010006
CR Motor over current
00010007
CR Motor in-position time-out
0001000A
CR axis detection error
0001000F
CR Motor PWM output faulty
0001001D
CR servo parameter error
The T-Fence may also be dirty or out of the carriage encoder. Check to make sure it is clean and in the center of the encoder. Contact Epson for additional assistance.
The current firmware corrects erroneous Service Request 00010007, which occurs after the power is first turned on. You can download this firmware upgrade from www.prographics.epson.com.

Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: Why are there only three cartridges in the black ink conversion kit?
faqs.answer: The ink conversion process drains only the black ink channel; the C/M/Y colors are not drained. The three cartridges in the conversion kit are used to close the C/M/Y ink valves during the draining process. However, the process performs an initial fill on the whole ink system after the draining is complete.

faqs.question: Do the Epson UltraChrome K3 inks have less outgassing than the previous Epson UltraChrome Inks?
faqs.answer:
The new Epson UltraChrome K3 inks have about the same outgassing as the previous ink set. So, depending upon the environmental conditions, Epson recommends that you let your prints “outgass” into interleaving papers (Epson Singleweight Matte, Doubleweight Matte, and Presentation Matte all make great interleaving papers) for at least 48 hours before framing.
Please note: You must replace the interleaving paper at the 24 hour mark with a fresh sheet. Proper framing procedures must be used, including no contact between the print and the inside of the glass or UV acrylic.

faqs.question: Do I need to drain the ink cartridges before transporting my product?
faqs.answer: No. The printer has mechanical ink valves that close when the ink levers are lifted up. For transportation, 110 ml ink cartridges (expended or full) should be installed in each ink slot and both ink levers should be raised to their up position.

faqs.question: How long does it take to switch between black modes on my product?
faqs.answer: Less than ten minutes.

faqs.question: Does my product have a pressurized ink delivery system?
faqs.answer: No.

faqs.question: How much ink is used during the switching of black ink modes?
faqs.answer:
The amount of ink flushed through the printer in the switching process varies, but we estimate the total ink usage (all cartridges combined) to be between 88 ml and 117 ml per switch.
Switching from one black mode to another (for example, from Photo Black to Matte Black) does use a significant quantity of ink. Part of it is used to flush all of the old ink type out of the printer's tubing, damper, and head, and to prime those components with a sufficient amount of the new ink type. As part of the switching process, the printer also flushes a smaller amount of each of the other colors through the print head in order to prepare the head for printing again. All this is performed in order to ensure high-quality prints in the new mode after the switch.

faqs.question: I'm getting a crease in my roll media. What should I do?
faqs.answer: A crease in roll media is the result of the paper feed roller holding the media for a long time. Remove the roll media from the paper path when you have finished using it to prevent the media from being creased.

faqs.question: My product recently started having trouble loading paper. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
You may need to clean the pickup rollers. Do the following:
Turn on the printer and remove any loaded paper.
Remove the paper tray so you can see the pickup rollers and roller covers.
Note
: The left side pickup roller may be in a different location than shown above, since it moves with the left side paper guide.
Clean the light grey areas beneath the roller covers.
We recommend using cotton swabs dampened with water to clean dust from the rollers. Be sure to allow ample time for the rollers to dry before loading paper.
To clean each roller's surface completely, they must be rotated. Press the
down arrow button on the printer's control panel to rotate the rollers; watch for a moment to see how the gears inside the printer are engaged when the rollers are moving. Be careful not to get anything stuck in between the rollers.
Rotate the rollers a little at a time, cleaning the exposed roller surface between rotations.

faqs.question: How can I prevent paper from jamming or misfeeding from the paper tray?
faqs.answer:
Fan the paper and tap it on a flat surface to even the edges.
If you need to add paper to the paper tray, first remove all paper from the tray and then add paper to the removed stack.
If your paper is curled, flatten it before you load it. If it curls excessively and jams frequently, stop using it.
Load the sheets with the printable side face down and the right edge of the paper resting against the right side of the paper tray. Make sure the sheets lie flat on the bottom of the tray.
Do not over-fill the paper tray.
When you load sheets of paper, place the edge of the paper against the right inner corner of the paper tray. Otherwise, printing may become misaligned.
Adjust the paper guide and edge guide according to the paper size. They must be snug against the paper.
Put the paper guide roller down and replace the paper tray cover.

faqs.question: What does the 250 stand for in the Epson driver Media Type setting?
faqs.answer: The 250 designation represents the paper weight (250 gsm). Make sure you select the 250 Media Type setting if the media installed in the printer is 250 gsm (roll paper). If there is a mismatch in paper weight, print quality may be affected by horizontal banding or other problems.

faqs.question: If I don't use roll paper do I need to have the roll paper holder attached?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will work without the roll paper holder installed. The holder is designed to be removed easily.

faqs.question: Which Epson media types produce the highest Dmax or L* value?

faqs.question: When I print on roll paper, my image prints too far to the left. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the black paper stop (flange) of the roll paper spindle is installed on the left side of the printer, when you face the printer. The flanges are color coded to match the spindle holders on the printer.

faqs.question: How do I create a borderless print with roll media from my Mac?
faqs.answer:
To print borderless on roll media, create a custom paper size in the driver and follow the guidelines below to determine the width parameter.  The method you use depends on the size of your media.
If you're using 10-, 12-, 13-, 14-, or 17-inch wide media and you want to use the
Auto Expand
option, enter a paper width setting that matches the actual width of your roll. For example, if you're using a 17-inch wide roll, enter 17 inches.
If you're using 10-, 12-, 13-, 14-, or 17-inch wide media and you want to use the
Retain Size
option, you'll need to increase two width parameters.  First, increase the image width by .34 inches (using your image editing software).  Then, make the paper width setting .23 inches larger than the actual width of your roll. For example, if you're using a 17-inch wide roll, enter 17.23 inches for the paper width.
If you're using 16-inch wide media, set the paper width to 16 inches. You can then select either the
Retain Size
or
Auto Expand
option.
For any size roll media, follow these tips to ensure correct borderless printing:
Make sure you set all page margins to zero.
When you use either the
Auto Expand
or
Retain Size
option, always add 0.1 inches to the length/height of your page size.
Selecting the
Auto Expand
option minimizes image clipping in your printout.

faqs.question: What kind of spray coating should I use to protect my canvas prints?
faqs.answer:
Epson has conducted limited internal testing of third-party over-coatings.  This testing indicates that the following third-party over-coatings help protect a print against the effects of water.
Make sure the media has cured for at least 24 hours or longer before using any spray coatings. The following products have been tested with our Canvas Papers:
Premier Art Print Shield (Tested by Wilhelm Imaging Research).
SureGuard Clear Gloss-McDonald-Pro-Tecta-Cote # 911
For complete specifications and additional information, please contact the manufacturer directly.
Note: Epson does not endorse any particular over-coating and does not guarantee the results. Epson does not make any claim as to the stability or longevity of these spray products.

faqs.question: How can I prevent smeared ink and droplets on my printouts?
faqs.answer:
The print head can gather dust over time, which then gathers ink. This accumulated ink can get deposited on the substrate during printing. Cleaning the wiper blade and pump cap assembly can solve this problem. Do the following:
Turn off the printer.
Open the top cover and press the cutter solenoid down to release the print head.
Note
: This photo shows the Pro 4800 cutter solenoid assembly; the assembly in the Pro 4000 is black.
Move the print head to the left.
Locate the wiper blade and clean it with a moist cotton swab.
Note
: Most of the wiper blade is located behind the clear plastic shield, which may be difficult to clean. If you use a long cotton swab you'll be able to reach further back and clean the blade more thoroughly. The blade is split down the middle so be sure to clean both sides of the blade and inside the split.
Inspect the foam pad area of the pump cap assembly for any large pieces of debris and gently remove them with a moist cotton swab. Then use the swab to gently wipe the topside frame of the plastic housing that holds the multi-colored foam pad.
Caution
: Do not try to remove the foam pad.
The flushing box next to the multi-colored cap assembly does not typically come in contact with the print head, but you should gently clean any debris that may have accumulated there.
Close the top cover and turn on the printer.
Print a
nozzle check
and inspect the printed pattern.
If the nozzle check pattern looks good, you are ready to print; you don't need to continue with the following steps.
If the nozzle check pattern is not satisfactory, continue with the next step.
If the nozzle check pattern is not satisfactory, run a cleaning cycle and print another nozzle check. In the printer utility, be sure to select
Print
(not
Auto
) for the nozzle check.
If the nozzle check pattern is still not complete, repeat step 9 until you see a good nozzle check pattern or you have run three cleaning cycles.
If the nozzle check pattern looks good, you are ready to print.
If the nozzle check pattern still is not good after running three cleaning cycles, contact Epson Technical Support for further assistance.

Make sure you use the correct profile settings.

faqs.answer: Print a nozzle check pattern. If you see gaps in the nozzle check pattern, run three cleaning cycles, then print another nozzle check pattern to see if all nozzles print now. If you still see gaps, run a power cleaning cycle.

faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: How can I share my product with other users?
faqs.answer:
We recommend sharing your printer via an Ethernet connection with the optional Epson High Speed Ethernet Print Server card (part number C12C824341 or C12C824052). This method provides many benefits, including better performance, over selecting

faqs.question: When should I use the product profiles that end in PK and MK?
faqs.answer: The PK profile should be used when photo black ink is installed in the printer. The MK profile should be used when matte black ink is installed in the printer.

faqs.question: Why should I use the Matte Black mode?
faqs.answer: The standard Photo Black ink has been optimized for RC and Photographic grade media types. If you're printing on matte-type papers such as Epson Velvet Fine Art, Enhanced Matte, or UltraSmooth Fine Art, your black density is significantly better when using Matte Black ink (and worth the switch).

faqs.question: Why have my pre-defined paper settings changed?
faqs.answer: If you name a custom paper setting using the same name as a pre-defined paper (like A4), the pre-defined paper settings are overwritten by the custom settings.

faqs.question: What does the Common Updater 7.0 file do?
faqs.answer: The Common Updater 7.0 file provides the latest Mac OS X 10.6 support for your printer driver. Before installing the updater, make sure the most current version of the Mac OS X 10.5 or 10.6 printer driver is installed on your computer. Restart your computer after installing the updater.

faqs.question: What is the Epson Advanced Black & White Printing Mode?
faqs.answer: This is a proprietary Epson screening and color management technology designed specifically to produce professional level black and white prints. The math behind this unique screen technology takes advantage of our three level black technology along with Yellow, Light Cyan, and Light Magenta to produce professional black and white prints from either color or grayscale files. Epson's new Advanced Black and White printing technology is simply another tool or alternative for professionals to use towards achieving the ultimate black and white print.

faqs.question: I cannot print from an application when using the ColorBurst RIP on a Windows 64-bit operating system. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The following two print options are available when using the ColorBurst RIP on a Windows 64-bit operating system:
Drag and drop method. Dragging and dropping a file into the ColorBurst queue window will send the print job to the printer. Only files with JPEG, TIFF, PDF, and EPS extensions can be printed using this method.
Open a file directly from ColorBurst. To print using this method, open the
File
menu, select
Open
, then browse for the file you need to print. Only files with JPEG, TIFF, PDF, EPS extensions can be printed using this method.

faqs.question: What is the Super (X) setting in the Epson driver?
faqs.answer: This is a Super Microweave setting that enables the print head to perform 8 microweave passes instead of the standard 4 passes. The through-put is slowed with this setting. However, it produces the highest quality prints when you use it along with the highest print resolutions of 1440 or 2880 with the high speed setting turned off.

faqs.question: What does the Remote Panel utility do?

Perform power cleanings
Set the printer clock
Set media counter settings

faqs.question: Why are only matte media types displayed in the driver's media list?
faqs.answer: When matte black ink is installed in the printer, only matte media types are displayed in the driver list.  The complete media list appears only when the photo black ink cartridge is installed.

faqs.question: What is the maximum image length I can print from Photoshop CS/CS2 with the standard Epson driver in Mac OS X?
faqs.answer:
The maximum image length is determined by the resolution of the image. An image cannot exceed 30,000 pixels in either direction (width or length). You can check the pixel count of an image by opening the Image menu in Photoshop and selecting
Image size
.
Examples:
For a 300 dpi image, the maximum length will be 100 inches (300 x 100 = 30,000).
For a 240 dpi image, the maximum length will be 125 inches (240 x 125 = 30,000).

faqs.question: Why are some of the paper types grayed out?
faqs.answer: The paper path you have selected determines which media types are available. If some media types are grayed out, that means these media types can only by used with one of the manual feed (front or rear) or roll feed methods.  The driver grays out these media types because using them from the paper tray may cause damage to the paper coating.

faqs.question: Why does the platen gap setting on my product revert back to Standard when my product is powered off/on?
faqs.answer:
The platen gap setting defaults back to
Standard
when the printer is powered off/on to prevent print quality problems that may occur if the platen gap is accidentally left at a wider setting.

faqs.question: Which connection enables my product to operate at full speed?
faqs.answer: All connections allow the printer to operate at full print engine speed. (The USB port must be 2.0 compatible.) Your CPU is the biggest factor in print engine speed.

faqs.question: Is there an optional TUMI cover available for my product?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tumi has made a custom, fitted printer cover for the Epson Stylus Pro 4800 using its patented Fusion Z Nylon Technology. It is available now and can be purchased from the Epson Store.

faqs.question: How do I get service for my product I purchased in another country?
faqs.answer: Due to differences in products sold in other countries, printers need to be serviced in the country of origin.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
